title: Art Museum of Southeast Texas

services.name: Current Exhibitions
services.desc: The Art Museum of Southeast Texas continues its 75th Anniversary celebration with A Legacy of Collecting: Art Museum of Southeast Texas, the second exhibition in a two-part series exploring the museum’s history through its permanent collection. Spanning 1987 to the present, the exhibition brings together selected artworks, archival photographs, and stories from the artists, supporters, museum professionals, and community members who have helped shape AMSET over the past four decades. The exhibition opens with a recap gallery, where visitors can revisit the museum’s first 37 years and view a video tour of A Legacy of Collecting: Beaumont Art Museum, the first exhibition in the series. services.name: Art After School
services.desc: In collaboration with the Beaumont Independent School District, AMSET’s Art After School program brings fourth graders from area Title I elementary schools (Martin Elementary, Fletcher Elementary, Charlton-Pollard Elementary, and Dr. Mae Jones-Clark Elementary) to AMSET. A school bus transports the students to the museum and then to their homes accompanied by a teacher’s aide from their school. A very popular and successful program, Art After School has a 99% participation level. During the week-long program, students complete workshops introducing them to museums and the work of our exhibiting artists. services.name: Schedule a Tour
services.desc: Advanced middle school art students from Odom Academy, the Beaumont Independent School District arts magnet, make 10 to 12 visits per school year to the Art Museum of Southeast Texas to take part in this program. At AMSET, Odom Junior Docents (OJDs) learn about museum practices and interact with exhibits and artists. The Junior Docents also create their own artwork and participate in a framing workshop with the Education and Curatorial Departments. Their artwork is then displayed each spring in AMSET’s Quinn Lecture Hall. blurb: The Art Museum of Southeast Texas is pleased to present Samantha Harrison: Land and Light as its Fall 2026 Community Art exhibition. Harrison is a self-taught painter and photographer. Her work is shaped by a love of travel and the natural world. Inspired by Georgia O’Keeffe, Ansel Adams, and Bauhaus design, she creates work based on places both real and imagined.
